item.content:encoded:
Hi there! I'm Gattebara, any pronouns, live in the Buryatia Republic, in Russia. I've known about the Foundation a long time ago, last year I joined the Russian branch, and now I've entered the original site. My purposes here are reading, voting and translation activity, I'm not a very good writer.

I am a huge fan of the Foundation, and reading some Sarkicism articles literally made me a leftist pro-feminist and defined many character traits and interests in me, uh oh. Well, maybe not so directly.

my other interests, although i don't think it's important: history, culture of other nations, various religions, young-adult books, music and She-Ra.

a random thought keep me up at night: why there are only two islands around Tallinn, but a lot of them near Helsinki….

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Hey. EponymousRex. Occasionally go by SteelGriffin or Griff sometimes. Long time reader, first time proper official poster. Heh, fiddled around with discussion the old IRC a fair number of years ago. Wanted to write someone/something as a comical doom magnet. Some poor dude attracting suffering enough to make him hate his pitiful existence, but never enough to end it. As if that hasn't been done to death, and honestly I'm surprised I remember it. Oh well.

I might try to do something more than read and so on, but probably not for awhile. Not until I'm over my anxiety and general cowardice.

I always found the Idea beyond the SCP setting, and the general mechanics of it as a collectively written universe to be fascinating. A massive cooperative writing project that has produced something so wonderful and thought provoking, not to mention Fun. So not only am I here for the stories, I'm here to watch the community, and I'm kicking myself for not deciding to become involved sooner.

Anyway to answer the question prompt. Despite my previous noting on my own anxieties, that rarely keeps me up that much. It's more just… My mind gets going on some idea, some story, some THING I want to write, create, etc. Though I do worry. About Family, about the future, all that crap. You know how it is.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone, I am very grateful to be a part of this site. I first discovered SCP when I saw a new uploaded video on Youtube at the time SCP-087 in very early 2012. I downloaded the game and played it, I also did a Google search that led me to the article and wow, this website has come a long way and I have finally made the effort to officially join after almost 9 years. I hope you are all doing well!

I am an avid reader and do plan to stay that way for quite some time but I have had some personal suggestions for SCPs but I haven't put the plans into action.

My hobbies are listening to music, watching anime, and playing video games.

As for the question, my answer is: Embarrassing things I did when I was a kid.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Hello!
I started reading SCPs over a decade ago, and considered joining but was intimidated at the time by all the info on what to do and not do when joining, submitting, etc.
I recently rediscovered it. I love fantasy and scifi, and this is replacement therapy for my D&D group during Covid lockdown (this is also a great source of potential magical objects/enemies for homebrew campaigns).
I don't have any plans to write for the site in the immediate future, but I was reading SCP 351 and enjoyed it so much I joined to upvote it.

To answer the monthly question, what keeps me up at night is climate change. I can't help but feel like the world we live in right now will seem like some strange fantasy in a couple decades. We always think of disasters happening to other people in distant - and often poor - countries, but honestly none of us are safe.

Hello folks, I am TruckRail82. I have been a lurker on the wiki for about 1 and a half years now, just reading articles and tales. item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Salutations. Long time, first time. I plan to read and possibly vote and offer feedback. I've been away from this site for a while. When I came back, there was a Series 6! I thought to myself, "hey, you mostly stick to old, proven works, why not jump into new stuff?" So I did. Then I thought, "if you really like some of these articles, why not join so you can offer some feedback?" And now I'm writing this.

"When is the last time it rained?" I've never experienced a drought nor do I live in an area where droughts really happen. Nevertheless, when that thought pops into my mind I have to try and figure out the last time there was rainfall or I cannot sleep.

Ahola! I've been lurking for a few years now and didn't really think about making an account until today. What drove me to do it was a godawful article that's so bad I wanted to downvote it. It was something about cardboard box man-spiders. Crazy, huh? Can't find it now but it's been marked for deletion, which is appropriate. I even had a couple ideas to improve on it but I'm still not familiar with the rules on rewriting deleted articles though.

I'm just going to be a casual reader/reviewer for now but if I ever get to writing an article/tale, I'll be in your care!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Hi Johnnyblushoes!

Welcome to the site! Happy to have you here! Nice to hear that you already have some ideas for both here and the WL, I wish you luck with developing them. A good place to start is by reading recent content to get a feel for each site and what does well there, so I've left you with my reading list to help get you started. Take things at whatever pace works best for you though, and enjoy your time here!

In regards to your question, yes, you are more than welcome to create your own characters for your tales/articles. In fact, pretty much every character is or at least started as someone's original character before being absorbed by the site. I wouldn't be too worried about stepping on people's toes, but it's better to be safe than sorry. If there is a specific character you want to write about, I'd recommend reading other pieces they're featured in, and seeing if the original author has anything to say about said character. Feel free to reach out if you have any further questions.

+Here are some places to start.
-Hope this helps!

Maybe you've already seen these before, maybe you haven't, but hopefully something here is of use to you. Of course, if you have any questions, feel free to reach out!

The newest, freshest material can be found on the Most Recently Created page. If that updates a little too frequently for you though and you want more of a look at what remains popular, you can also try the Top Rated New Pages.

If you want to see what other folks in the community like, there's the User-Curated Lists. Here you can find things the community has put together and deemed a good read. Or maybe you want to give some underrated articles some love? Try out the Underread and Underrated page.

Enjoy large hubs and working your way through them? Some cool hubs include the Guide Hub for things that cover the Site itself, Site News Hub for updates on all sorts of monthly Site content, Canon Hub for all the various canons, GoI Format Hub for all your GoI needs, and Tales Hub for your favorite tales.

Finally, if you find an author you love from any of this and want to see more from them, you can find them in the Authors' Pages section. If they're not on that list, try the statistic site, scpper.com.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Howdy! I stumbled upon the Foundation a few years ago via a simple google search. (Who would've thought?) Since then, the Foundation has endlessly inspired me and I regularly discuss it with the handful of fellow skippers I know in real life. I'm so grateful that I actually took the time to become a member.

Currently, I plan to read, comment, vote and–when I have a little more experience under my belt–review. Me and my friend (who, despite my best efforts, is not yet a member of this site) have an idea for an SCP in the works, but it's still in the very early stages.

For the monthly question: I often lay awake at night, pondering my future career. Also, I must confess that I have a habit of watching SCP Illustrated immediately before bed, and I'm sure you can imagine how that turned out.

Overall, I am extremely happy and proud to call myself a member of this amazing site! See you around!

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Note: If you're going to introduce yourself here, please scroll down and click "New Post" and NOT "reply", otherwise your comment will nest incorrectly!

Hello, readers and reviewers of the Foundation Universe!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

Let's start off with some things to take a look at to enhance your reading, now that you're a site member:

  • If you have any questions about the Foundation'verse and its various individuals and groups of interest, head over to the Foundation Universe forum to talk about the various aspects of living/working/being in constant fear of a world where anomalies are real.
  • Did you know our site has a night mode version? If you're interested in that (and a few other neat things!), check out our Usertools page.
  • Want to leave a comment or read others' thoughts on something you've read recently? Scroll down to the bottom of that page you read, click the "Discuss" link, and take a look at the comments others have posted!

For those looking to put your knowledge of the SCP-verse to work and contribute to the site by helping develop works-in-progress, head on over to the Writing Help forums!

  • So you want to be a concept reviewer?
  • So you want to be a draft reviewer?
  • And of course, remember the Criticism Policy!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Go ahead and respond to other new members if you find that your interests overlap, and definitely ask for reading suggestions if there's a particular kind of SCP article or tale you enjoy reading. If you're looking to get started as a critiquer, feel free to mention the kind of material you particularly want to see more of on the wiki! You might even see some of our authors drop by here from time to time, if you mention you liked their work! :)

Welcome to the site!
